title: Why the World's Biggest Business Competition Pays for Revenue, Not Pitches
summary: The World's Biggest Business Competition pays $1M across 181 winners, and eligibility is earned through verified revenue, not a pitch. Here is how the rule works.
body_markdown:
The World's Biggest Business Competition puts $1M in prizes on the table, and you qualify by making real money, not by delivering the best pitch. Simon Squibb's four-week programme rewards founders who ship a live product that earns, with prize eligibility gated on verified revenue during the run. Emergent powers the[App Builder track](https://emergent.sh/ai-contests/worlds-biggest-business-competition) , where founders build that revenue-ready product with no code needed.


## The prize, by the numbers


The prize pool is $1M, shared across 181 winners. One grand prize takes $100,000, and 180 runners-up take $5,000 each. The competition ends with a live Demo Day finale after the four-week build phase.

## Why eligibility is earned through revenue


You become prize-eligible by generating verified revenue during the programme, not by pitching an idea to a panel. That single rule reshapes the whole competition. A polished deck counts for nothing on its own. A live product that takes a real payment is the thing that qualifies you.


Most business competitions reward the best story in the room. This one rewards the founder who built something people actually pay for. The design favours builders who ship over presenters who promise, which is why the entry bar is a working business rather than a business plan. Full prize rules and selection criteria are set by the organiser and published in the official[terms and conditions](https://accelerator.helpbnk.com/terms) .


## What this means for App Builder entrants


Because the bar is real revenue, the App Builder track is built around getting you to a live, payment-taking product fast. On Emergent, you describe what you want in plain English, add Stripe, and deploy to a live URL, which is exactly what the revenue rule asks for. You can ship the same product to web, iOS, and Android from one chat, and you keep the codebase either way. Emergent's role in the track is covered in full in[this announcement](https://emergent.sh/news/emergent-backs-app-builder-track-worlds-biggest-business-competition) .


Entry is free, and registration is open now on the[official competition](https://worldsbiggestbusinesscompetition.com/wbbc-page) site. For more open and upcoming builder challenges, browse the[AI contests](https://emergent.sh/ai-contests) hub.
